extraction.notes: Read in full (pages 1-5). English original. The brief has no chapter structure; all items concern foreign nationals' (beneficiaries of temporary protection) access to Moldova's labour market and are tagged Chapter 2 (cluster 2, chapter 02), following the convention of the G3 sample files. No theme items. The brief is dated November 2025 on its pages; the register records March 2026 from the PDF metadata (to confirm); period_covered is left empty as in the register, and the survey data are the SERHC 2024 (methodology, page 4), given as the reference period of metrics. Page headers and footers ("Policy Brief #1 Republic of Moldova", "November 2025", photo credits) and the section labels are interleaved with the text in the conversion; quotes avoid them. Section names are taken from the nearest printed label; the opening summary on page 1 has no heading. Short document: claims repeated between the opening summary and the detailed pages are extracted at each place (rules section 5; M3 applies to long documents). Left out: the count of Ukrainians who sought refuge (page 1), humanitarian context; household income bands and access to credit (page 2) and the recommendations to expand childcare services and microfinance (page 4), as general integration and financial inclusion rather than labour-market access; the methodology, acknowledgements and contacts (pages 4-5). Internal inconsistencies for pass 2, recorded as printed: paid work since arrival 29 percent (pages 1, 2, 3) against 34 percent (page 3); job seekers citing language 36 percent (pages 1, 2) against "nearly half" (page 2); experience and education 80 and 77 percent (page 2) against 81 and 76 percent (page 3). For the analyst: the childcare and wages barriers (-0016, -0017) are kept as stated barriers to employment; the analyst may treat them as outside the Chapter 2 boundary. Second-pass check (PC-05) by checker-GOV8c on 5 November 2026: 2 items added (review/RUN-2026-02/second_pass/MDA-IO-2026-002.csv).
